definition: Swift's ability to work out a value's type from the value you assign, so `let cups = 3` is an `Int` without an annotation. The type is fixed from then on.
A Foundation number type that stores base-10 digits exactly, which makes it the right choice for money. Unlike `Double`, adding 0.1 ten times gives exactly 1.
A type such as `Decimal?` that holds either a value or `nil`. Swift won't let you use it as a plain value until you unwrap it safely.
A statement that unwraps an optional or checks a condition and must exit the scope in its `else` branch. After it, the unwrapped value is available for the rest of the function.
The `??` operator, which returns the value inside an optional or a default when the optional is `nil`, as in `note ?? "No note"`.
Writing `!` after an optional to take its value without checking. If the optional is `nil`, the app crashes immediately, so use it only when `nil` would be a programmer error.
Swift's rule that a `switch` must handle every possible value. Over enums it makes the compiler list every switch you need to update when you add a case.
A block of code without a name that can be stored, passed to functions like `filter` or `map`, and called later. It captures the variables it uses from its surrounding scope.
The behaviour of structs and enums: assigning or passing a value makes an independent copy, so changing the copy never affects the original.
The behaviour of classes and actors: assigning an instance copies a reference, so several names can point at the same object and see each other's changes.
A keyword on struct and enum methods that change the value's own properties. Mutating methods can only be called on a `var`, never on a `let`.
Two objects, or an object and a closure, holding strong references to each other so neither can be freed by ARC. Capturing `[weak self]` in the closure breaks the cycle.
Data attached to a specific enum case for each instance, such as `case card(lastFour: String)`. You read it back with pattern matching like `case .card(let lastFour)`.
A fixed `String` or number stored for each case of an enum declared like `enum Category: String`. `init(rawValue:)` converts back and returns `nil` for unknown values.
A named set of requirements, such as properties and methods, that structs, classes and enums can adopt. Code written against the protocol works with every conforming type.
An extension on a protocol that provides default implementations, so every conforming type gains that behaviour without writing it again.
Swift 6 syntax such as `throws(BudgetError)` that names the exact error type a function can throw, so callers can switch over the error exhaustively without a catch-all.
A method like `.padding()` or `.font(.headline)` that wraps a SwiftUI view in a new view with a change applied. Modifiers apply in order, so their order matters.
A SwiftUI property wrapper that stores a value the view owns outside the view struct, so it survives re-renders and triggers an update when it changes.
A two-way connection to a value owned elsewhere, written with a `$` prefix. Controls such as `Toggle` and `TextField` take bindings so they can read and write the source of truth.
A macro from the Observation framework that makes a class's properties trackable, so SwiftUI re-renders only the views whose body read a property that changed.
A SwiftUI container that pushes and pops screens. `NavigationLink(value:)` selects a value and `.navigationDestination(for:)` decides which screen shows it.
Running async work as child tasks, with `async let` or task groups, that must finish before their parent returns. Cancelling the parent cancels every child automatically.
A reference type that protects its mutable state by running one call at a time. Code outside the actor must use `await` to reach it, which prevents data races.
A protocol marking types that are safe to pass between concurrency domains. Structs made of Sendable values qualify automatically; plain classes with mutable properties don't.
An attribute that isolates code or a type to the main actor, the main thread where UI runs. New Xcode app projects make it the default isolation.
The combination of `Decodable` and `Encodable`, which lets the compiler generate code to convert your types to and from formats such as JSON.
A macro that turns a class into persisted SwiftData data. You read models with `@Query` and insert or delete them through the model context, which autosaves.
Apple's testing framework where tests are functions marked `@Test`, checked with `#expect` and `#require`, and parameterized with `arguments:`.
Apple's beta distribution service. Builds uploaded to App Store Connect reach up to 100 internal testers immediately and up to 10,000 external testers after Beta App Review.
